Speech. Wake-word listening uses Vosk, the small English model vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15, by Alpha Cephei. The library and the model are Apache License 2.0. Your voice stays on the phone. The ear is English, so say the English command words. The spoken warnings can still use the language you picked. Pictures. The camera uses a small YOLO model trained for this app. It can speak people, bicycles, motorcycles, cars, buses, trucks, cows, dogs, cats, auto-rickshaws, cycle rickshaws, handcarts, potholes, open drains, curbs, stairs, poles, barriers, street objects, trees, chairs, couches, tables, beds, toilets, plants, refrigerators, televisions, and doors. Speed bump and low branch are not included. Curb pictures are few, so curbs are easy to miss. Depth. Walls and unnamed close objects use Depth Anything V2 Small, Apache License 2.0. The number is relative depth, not meters. Calibrate distance on this phone. Glass doors and glass walls are often missed. If this phone already has ARCore with depth, that map is used instead. This app does not download ARCore. Picture sources. ROD: Amirkabir University of Technology, Zandi and colleagues, MIT, from Roboflow sets that are mostly CC BY 4.0. RDD2022 India potholes: Arya and colleagues, Geoscience Data Journal 2024, CC BY 4.0. Open Images, including doors, stairs, street lights, carts, and cattle: annotations CC BY 4.0, Flickr photos CC BY 2.0. COCO 2017 indoor pictures: annotations CC BY 4.0. Those photos are from Flickr and are not all cleared for commercial use. Roboflow pothole sets, CC BY 4.0. Tuk-tuk and rickshaw pictures via shravya11, CC BY 4.0. Datacluster Labs auto-rickshaw sample, CC BY 4.0 on the dataset card. AssistEye road obstacles: MIT for the collection. Some upstream pictures are CC0 or CC BY 4.0. Some curb pictures in that collection carry stock-photo watermarks and are not redistributed. This app is an extra to a white cane. It is not a replacement.
